questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃COCH₂CH(OH)CH₃ is
questions.explain: The ketone outranks the alcohol, so it takes the suffix -one with the lowest locant (C-2), and –OH becomes the prefix hydroxy at C-4.

questions.q: Which of these groups has the highest priority for choosing the IUPAC suffix?
questions.explain: The order runs ester > acyl halide > amide > nitrile > isocyanide > aldehyde, so the ester group is the principal group here.

questions.q: Which group is always cited as a prefix and never as a suffix?
questions.explain: Nitro, halo, alkoxy, alkyl and phenyl groups never take a suffix. –OH, –NH₂ and –SH can be suffixes (-ol, -amine, -thiol) when they are the principal group.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of CH₃O–CO–CH₂CH₂–COOH is
questions.explain: –COOH outranks the ester, so the name ends in -oic acid with the COOH carbon as C-1; the ester end at C-4 is written as the prefixes methoxy and oxo. Naming it as an ester ignores the priority order.
